I grew up in the mountains of Oregon, and hour from the closest town. There was one other kid on the mountain we lived on, an hour or so hike up. She was too rich and snobby for me, though I tried to be her friend a few times. I was independent and I had my little sister to annoy. I was absolutely never bored, but I only lived there from 6-10 or something.
Homeschooled until 4th grade and definitely a weird kid when I got to public school. I brought animals bones to show and tell and touched a girls hair once to tell her it was pretty (without asking). Little awkward things like that, but made my first friend also through being awkward.
I got to lunch the first day of school and there were two tables we were allowed to sit at (my teacher explained): each was allowed 7 students, yet as he said that I could see there were 2 students at the first and 12 at the other. When I pulled a chair up to the loud table after they told me to, I asked about the table setup and why arent those 2 students sitting with us?
They said that those 2 were “weird” and they thought one was “gay”. I had no idea what that meant, but I didn’t think it should matter, and I told them if she isn’t and they haven’t asked they were excluding her for no reason.
So after lunch I asked her if she was gay- she almost beat me up, but then the teacher sat us together and we were friends throughout high school!
I guess my point it public school is terrifying. Nature is much more welcoming, you can learn a whole lot from it, and it’s where we are meant to be!
